freeze.text: Feature Freeze Declared. Our Features are LOCKED for v0.11.0.

ship_list.title: No high-severity bug open
ship_list.note: A high-severity bug holds the release. Medium ones may land after the freeze.

ship_list.title: Every feature merged, moved or cut
ship_list.note: The freeze is declared: an open feature needs an exception, or moves to the next minor.

ship_list.title: Code-review findings closed
ship_list.note: A blocking finding stays on the milestone. The rest move to the next minor.

ship_list.title: Performance issues closed
ship_list.note: Issues labelled `performance`. A regression against the cycle's baselines is a bug for this milestone; the others may move to the next minor.

ship_list.title: Pull requests merged
ship_list.summary: 7 open: 1 ready (longest 1 h), 6 draft, 1 failing checks

ship_list.title: main green for 24 hours
ship_list.note: The candidate needs every push check and nightly job green for a day, Heavy Checks' nightly run included.

ship_list.note: The candidate needs one on its exact commit.

ship_list.title: Candidate approved

#3169 Python 3.14 → 3.15 for the build tooling (agent:WSL).

[Security] On Linux, a root session run for a user reads config.toml and user themes by path, following the user's links
[Tracker] C++23 audit (main a6b09132): toolchain facts and findings
[Testing] Six Linux parsers of files other users or packages control have no fuzz harness (crontab, systemd unit files, XDG autostart, os-release, smaps_rollup, pressure)
[Testing] Windows has no fuzz presence: the version-resource walk, event-log XML, ETW UDP payload and SMART page parsers are unfuzzed, though they build on Linux
[Docs] Twenty comments that say something the code no longer does, several of them about thread safety or what a guard checks
[Docs] The user guide says every Linux session writes /tmp/tasksmack-debug.log, but a Linux root session writes /run/tasksmack/tasksmack-debug-<uid>.log
[Perf] The sessions feed's sampler isn't told to stop at AppExitingEvent, so its join still waits after the Processes sampler's

[Perf] LinuxDiskProbe lists /sys/block and reads every device's size and slaves/ on each sample since #4596, about 3x the read's cost, so main's Heavy Checks benchmark gate is red
[Refactor] The elevated code's security helpers: one static TrustedInstaller SID, HandleRelativeFile trusts it, one trailing-separator path compare (#4368 follow-up)

recently_closed.title: [BUG] Core::readWholeFile takes a failed read part-way as the end of the file, so a config.toml whose read errors loads cut short or empty as if it were whole
[BUG] Windows: about fifteen OS resources are released by hand with allocating calls in between, so an allocation failure leaks them
[Refactor] The elevated Windows code keeps private copies of the same security helpers, and the copies have drifted
[BUG] In a setcap session, programs TaskSmack starts inherit its scrubbed environment: no GTK_IM_MODULE or GIO/GDK/GTK module paths, and Mesa's shader cache and SDL's libdecor switched off
[BUG] Windows dumpFileStem() passes an image name that is not valid UTF-8 through unchanged
[BUG] Revert guard: a changed path containing a space keeps git's trailing TAB on the ---/+++ header, so git blame fails and the whole PR goes unchecked
[BUG] A dump folder whose name isn't valid UTF-8 is used for one dump only; the next dump goes back to the saved or default folder
[BUG] Open file location skips the other-mount-namespace check for an executable marked (deleted), so a container process's replaced binary opens the host's same-named folder
[BUG] Every root-for-user save refusal is shown as "couldn't be opened ... TaskSmack is using its default settings", which is false for a symlinked or hard-linked config that loaded fine
[Security] Every session, root and setcap ones included, dlopen()s /opt/rocm/lib/librocm_smi64.so with no check of who could have put it there
[BUG] Power switches to the larger unit too early: 0.96 W prints "1.0 W" (was "960.0 mW") and 0.96 mW prints "1.0 mW"
[BUG] A stop's running-dependents guard still skips a dependent whose LoadUnit or ActiveState read times out, so the stop takes that running dependent down
[BUG] gen-unicode-case-fold.py leaves three CaseFolding.txt S mappings out of the simple-fold table (U+1FD3->U+0390, U+1FE3->U+03B0, U+FB05->U+FB06)
[Testing] RequestStopEndsTheThreadWithoutWaitingAndStopThenJoins cannot fail: stop() wakes and joins the thread itself, so a requestStop() that does nothing still passes
[Security] Every root session writes its Xauthority copy to the same tasksmack-xauthority file, so a second user's root session replaces the first one's cookies
[BUG] The libdecor configure checks read a header SDL writes only at generate time, so they never run on a fresh configure, including every release.yml build
[Security] Run as root for a user, TaskSmack's own PATH is still ROOT_PATH with /usr/local/sbin and /usr/local/bin first, so SDL's zenity dialog runs from the folders #4396 refuses
[Security] The Startup probe's share check misses NT "\??\" paths, so another account's scheduled task can still make an elevated TaskSmack open \??\UNC\host\share (gets around the #4374 fix)
[Security] As root, a dump folder on CIFS, NFS, 9p or another network filesystem passes the root-only check, though #4554/#4572 made the same filesystems untrusted for tools
[BUG] A ProcessModel refresh that throws part-way leaves mixed rate baselines, so the next sample's I/O, page-fault and power rates are inflated
[BUG] openLocalNtFile refuses every file on a FAT/FAT32 (and probably exFAT) volume: a failed FileAttributeTagInfo query is taken to mean "not local"
[Security] The elevated installer's Remove mode follows junctions inside a folder standard users can write, so a standard user can make it delete any file or folder as admin or SYSTEM
[Security] A signed old Uninstall.exe in a user-writable folder counts as trusted, and is then run elevated by path in that folder
[BUG] The Processes table's Name and Command columns sort by raw bytes, so "Émile" sorts after "Zoe"
[BUG] Generated CPack config files with the maintainer's local worktree paths were committed at the repo root (CPackConfig.cmake, CPackProjectConfig.cmake, CPackSourceConfig.cmake)
[Docs] The text-encoding rules in CONTRIBUTING.md and copilot-instructions.md contradict the UTF-8 audit's decisions D1 and D2 (#4299) in five places
[BUG] Missing tests for non-ASCII and invalid-input round trips of written files, dump names, config encodings and clipboard text
[BUG] Linux Open file location says 'inside a sandbox or container' whenever stat fails, e.g. root opening a user's AppImage (#4600)
[BUG] Shutdown path investigation
[BUG] One UDP map walk that runs out of steps shows a 'TCP only' warning and a published problem, though the next read recovers (#4602)
[Testing] Fuzz harnesses compile with no warnings, and the PR smoke build links libstdc++, where the libc++ hardening define does nothing
[BUG] Linux Storage lists optical drives, floppies, eMMC boot areas and empty nbd devices since disks come from /sys/block (#4596)
[BUG] Linux services: a dropped bus connection or systemd re-exec still counts as an answer, so a stop can skip the dependents check (#4595)
[BUG] Windows path and account identity comparisons fold ASCII only, not ordinal-ignore-case as Windows does
[BUG] measure-idle.ps1: the fresh config folder lets the startup access notice open over the measured window
[Tooling] measure-idle.sh runs TaskSmack on the user's real config, unlike measure-idle.ps1 and profile-perf.sh, despite CONTRIBUTING saying it waits as profile-perf does
[Docs] CONTRIBUTING.md says every profiling script emits KEY=value lines at exit; pgo.sh and ui-compare.sh don't
[Testing] pgo.sh, ui-compare.sh and ninja-build-profile.py have no tests
[Docs] The sanitizer suppression notes are stale: tsan.supp cites GoogleTest 1.15's pthread_barrier, and CONTRIBUTING.md describes one entry of each file
[Testing] profile-perf.sh (681 lines) has no tests
[Testing] UBSan runs its default group only: a division of a rate by a zero interval is never reported
[Testing] The fuzzers run under AddressSanitizer only, so signed overflow, bad shifts and misaligned loads in the parsers go unreported
[BUG] ProcessWatchWorkerTest.AWatchThatThrowsStopsTheSessionAndSaysWhy: ASan reports a stack-overflow under win-asan-ubsan
[Testing] The /proc readers behind 'may this root session trust SUDO_UID' have no test that names them
[Testing] StorageModelTest.PublicationDoesNotWaitForTheWriterToCopyHistory is flaky on the Linux release CI leg
[BUG] Linux Startup tab: a systemd user unit whose ExecStart begins with a specifier, a bare name or a quoted path is shown as 'program not found'
[BUG] A UDP map walk that hits its step limit counts as a complete reading, causing a false rate spike
[BUG] Linux: 'Open file location' shows a path from another mount namespace as if it were on this system (Flatpak apps, containers)
[BUG] Linux: the Connections tab names each socket's owner by re-opening /proc/<pid>/comm by number after the scan, so a reused PID shows another process's name
[BUG] Linux: LinuxDiskProbe decides 'whole disk' by the shape of the name, so md0, nbd0, rbd0 and pmem0 get no row
[BUG] Linux services: a timed-out property read counts as an answer, so a queued start is reported failed and a stop can skip the running-dependents guard
[BUG] Linux: DRMGPUProbe reads sysfs numbers with std::stoull, so a GPU temperature below 0 C becomes garbage; eight sysfs readers disagree on signs, trimming and failure
[Security] One descriptor is duplicated without close-on-exec, and no clang-tidy check guards the pattern (#2148, #3762 were the same class)
[BUG] Auto-unit formatters print '1024.0 KiB', '1000.0 mW' and '1000.0/s' just under a unit boundary
[BUG] Broker Writer::text() cuts strings at 64 KiB mid-code-point and doesn't mark them as cut
[BUG] Linux: TaskSmack won't start from a working directory that has been deleted
[BUG] Sha256::hashFile() treats a read error as end-of-file and returns the digest of a truncated file
[Security] Release builds leave local variables uninitialized; every tested build pattern-fills them
[Security] Windows builds ship with no standard-library hardening; Linux ships libc++'s
CI: main is red
[Security] stb_image is built with every decoder, though every caller wants PNG only; the icon size cap has no test
[Security] Linux: the INET_DIAG reply walker keeps its remaining length unsigned, so an unaligned final length wraps it and the walk reads stale buffer bytes
[Perf] Process filtering is 27-38% slower since Unicode case folding (#4492): BM_ProcessFilter_Indices against the Windows baseline
[BUG] Environment::escapeForDisplay writes \xNN and leaves backslashes unescaped, unlike D1's U+FFFD
